text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:
- The Swiss Federal Health Office is currently investigating the consequences of tobacco consumption on federal finances, Swiss Health Minister Ruth Dreifuss said.
- Delegates of the Swiss People's Party decided not to support a federal initiative to ban exports of Swiss arms.
- The Social Democrats were big winners in cantonal elections in the canton of Graubuenden as the party won three seats. The Swiss People's Party remained the strongest political power.

- The Social Democrats in Solothurn canton failed in a bid to obtain a second seat in the cantonal government. The old formula remained stable with two seats for the Radical Democrats, two for the Christian Democrats and one for the Social Democrats. - Delegates of the Swiss Freedom Party, formerly known as the Motorists Party, on Saturday announced that they would launch four public referendums under one theme 'fight traffic jams'.

- Philippe Joye, a member of the Geneva government, told Swiss television that he will not seek another term in office. Joye has acknowledged having had an affair with a 17-year-old man. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
